trivia: The title song is a Cécile McLorin Salvant original, written for her first album on Nonesuch, and the Brooklyn Youth Chorus is credited on it. Stereophile chose the album as its Album of the Month for April 2022, for both performance and sound quality.

title: Nightrider
composer: Tom Misch and Yussef Dayes with Freddie Gibbs, Miles James, Jordan Rakei, Syed Adam Jaffrey and Tom Driessler (per the Wikipedia track list)
original_issue: Beyond the Groove, Blue Note and Caroline (album What Kinda Music, 24 Apr 2020)
personnel: Tom Misch (guitar); Yussef Dayes (drums); Freddie Gibbs (rap vocal, featured guest). Musician credits by track are not itemised in the sources used
trivia: Rapper Freddie Gibbs is the only vocal guest on the album. Misch and Dayes, both from South London's contemporary jazz scene, met at the launch party for Misch's 2018 album Geography and built the record from jam sessions. They played this song at an NPR Tiny Desk (home) concert in July 2020, and the album reached number four in the UK.

notes: Recording year is uncertain: the album grew from jam sessions that started after the pair met in 2018 (one liner note places the decision to record in summer 2018), and no session dates were found, so the 24 Apr 2020 release year is used and the track could date from 2018 or 2019. Not tagged crossover: a Blue Note and Caroline release, both artists are described as part of South London's jazz scene, but the rap feature and neo-soul feel make it a judgment call. The composer field follows the Wikipedia track list, whose album header credits Misch and Dayes plus the noted contributors.
